newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - S&P smiles on the Philippines.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - S&P smiles on the Philippines.

text.p: Philippines bonds showed little reaction to news Standard and Poor's raised the country's ratings because the upgrade was so widely expected, traders said Friday.

"We haven't seen too much tightening in the secondary market because the upgrade was expected. It is just one more notch up the ladder for the Philippines, which has been trading up for a year," said Carlyle Peake, vice president at Merrill Lynch in Hong Kong.

S&P said it raised its rating on US$4.4 billion of the Philippines long-term foreign currency debt to BB-plus from BB. It also raised to BB-plus the ratings of National Power Corp, Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co and Bangko Sentra ng Pilipinas, the central bank.
The rating agency also raised the country's peso debt.
Merrill's Peake noted that many Philippine bonds already are trading like investment grade credits.
Many analysts expect the Philippines to be upgraded again fairly soon to investment grade.
S&P said the Philippines rating outlook remains positive.
Philippines Central Bank Governor Gabriel Singson said the country would immediately benefit from the upgrading because it is set to issue its 30-year/100-year Yankee bonds very soon.
With the upgrade, government-held Land Bank of the Philippines picked a good day to launch its US$200 million floating rate certificate of deposit issue.
The five-year paper pays an all-in return of 80.5 basis points, the tightest spread offered by a Philippine bank this years.
In other news, Standard Chartered Bank said it would issue a HK$2.0 billion FRCD.
